findings: Algolia's default typo tolerance and prefix matching made 210 of 212 Hacker News hits for 'matcha' words like match, matches and matching (research/commerce/hn-exact-match-probe.json); ECDEV's mention rule already excluded them from counts, but they spent 6 of the run's requests
With exact matching, Hacker News returns 2 genuine posts in 3 pages and exact per-slice totals

Bluesky's unauthenticated search serves its first page and refuses the next cursor (403): SOURCE_REFUSED_FURTHER_PAGES, temporal coverage about 0.15 of the window, as the earlier contract probe predicted
Mastodon tag timelines slice by status id and returned complete coverage; one reply tree was read complete
Every feed source (Google Trends JP, Mastodon trending tags, Bluesky trends, PR Times RDF, NHK RSS, a Mastodon tag record) ran live through ECDEV's runtime with no failures

Feeds were cut to 50 items while coverage claimed COMPLETE_BY_SOURCE: PR Times serves 200 items. Feeds are now read whole (up to 1000) and paged sources refuse a page larger than requested; the same live run then read 200 and 86 items and found 10 mentions instead of 1
A live call carried an unknown field that ECDEV accepted: tool arguments are now checked against each tool's declared input schema before it runs

Public product research ran live through ECDEV: robots consulted, both pages captured and hashed, prices extracted exactly, and both candidates held at INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE for lacking a cross-source identifier and a second site; PARTIAL reflects 50% field observability (no GTIN or weight on these pages)

Hypotheses from live snapshots were noise: refinements were a cluster's first five terms alphabetically (link hashes, image sizes, function words, kana particles) and every one-post cluster became a hypothesis (45 for 47 mentions). Content terms now drop links, refinements are terms shared by at least two of a cluster's posts and informative, only clusters of two or more posts that refine something become hypotheses, and the topic over every mention always comes first
Open: lexical clustering grouped 46 live posts into 45 clusters; the Jaccard 0.25 with two shared terms rule rarely joins real posts, which a labelled sample should tune rather than a guess

Bluesky refuses its next cursor, so one window read 50 posts and covered about 15% of 3 days; 6-hour slices, each served its first page, read 347 posts and covered 67% within 20 requests (10 of 12 slices; 8 ended below 50 posts, i.e. read completely)

With 12 requested slices and 10 affordable, the two oldest went unread; slices are now widened to fit the request budget (and the 31-slice cap), so the same 20 requests sampled every part of the window: 10 slices of 7.2 hours, 394 posts, 7 slices read completely and 3 reported partial at the page limit

Visible-text watching works live through ECDEV's monitor: on two store pages the raw bytes differed between captures while the visible-text fingerprint stayed identical, and no change was reported; raw-byte comparison would have raised a false change on every tick. A site whose robots crawl delay exceeds the fetch budget (Hacker News, 30 s) is refused with ROBOTS_DELAY_EXCEEDS_FETCH_BUDGET and recorded UNKNOWN, never as a change

A live matcha run (HN, Bluesky, Mastodon; 20 requests; 215 mentions; 2026-10-07) under the tuned clustering rule gave product leads (matcha latte, oat milk, sugar-free caramel, black sesame, dubai chocolate, brown sugar, ice cream, kindle cover) but also generic refinements (people who, feel like, know); after a hand-written general-word list was added to the informative filter, a fresh live run kept the product phrases and lost the generic ones, while weaker words (wasn't until, occasionally, saw) remain. Hypotheses are still leads to check, not demand

Sliced coverage counted only slices read to their end, so a Bluesky run whose six 12-hour slices each hit the 50-post page limit reported 0.0 coverage (printed -0.0, an empty float sum) for 248 posts. Raw Bluesky search pages come back newest first by post creation time (1 inversion in 248 posts; indexedAt order is not monotonic), so a slice cut short now covers its span back to its oldest item, as an unsliced query already did, and only the rest of it is a gap; the same live query then reported 0.539 and, in two later runs, 0.688

Live Bluesky slices failed about once per run as FETCH_NETWORK_ERROR. Classified through reqwest: 5 of 60 requests to api.bsky.app failed in the connect phase (connection reset after about 12 s), and the operator proxy's relay log shows the egress tunnel closing mid-handshake with only the client hello sent, so no request reached the source. One retry is now made for connect-phase failures only, never more, and recorded as connect_retries on the response; two later live runs had no failures, so the retry path itself was not exercised live

Hypothesis research actions searched the bare topic (matcha) rather than the hypothesis's own phrase, and listed single-word refinements such as 'matcha free' before 'matcha sugar-free caramel'. Product queries now run most specific first: recurring phrases (more authors, more posts, then a phrase naming the topic), then refinements no phrase holds, then the topic alone; live, actions now open with queries such as 'matcha chai latte' and 'matcha caramel protein'

Copied text inflated the matcha clusters: 11 exact copies and 35 near-copy pairs among 259 Bluesky posts, 24 pairs from one account, and one account's repeated 'vibe with coffee matcha nottingham' posts became a six-post hypothesis. Snapshots now carry text_copies (normalised character 5-gram Jaccard 0.8, or containment 0.9 for texts of 40+ characters, links removed; posts are grouped, never removed) and clusters carry distinct authors and texts. A live run (261 mentions, 248 distinct texts, 19 posts in 6 copy groups) excluded 8 clusters from hypotheses, each checked by hand: six were one account (a bot, a templated 'SPOTTED' account, a Kindle deals poster, an account posting one article twice) and two were one headline pasted by 2 and 5 accounts. Distinct texts are not proof of independent origin

Hypotheses had no keyless price source: research actions needed operator-supplied seed URLs. Open Prices (ODbL crowdsourced store prices with photo proofs) now runs through ecdev.price.observations; Open Food Facts' own product API is disallowed for every agent in its robots.txt and is not read. Live (2026-10-07, 8 requests each): 'matcha latte' found 15 priced products (Sugimoto organic matcha latte at a median USD 14.99 across 3 US stores from one contributor), 'oat milk' 29 with 7 substring-only matches such as Goat Milk excluded, 'matcha' 108 (Oatly Matcha Oat Drink: 14 prices in EUR, NOK, PLN and SEK). These are shelf prices from volunteers, not online listings or demand; record research/commerce/open-prices-contract.json

About a third of live matcha posts are not English (12 Spanish, 5 German, 5 Dutch, 4 French, 3 Portuguese among 259), and their function words became refinements ('el matcha', 'de mate', 'como con está'); @handles made 'bsky social' one. A closed list of articles, prepositions and conjunctions of those languages (leaving out words that are also English, such as die, den and pour) and @handle removal fixed both in a fresh live run (15 hypotheses; a Spanish cluster now refines to 'matcha kombucha'); the Hacker News cluster benchmark is unchanged (precision 0.957, recall 0.058). An unchecked edit was first lost to formatting and caught by this live check

Lexical clusters split one product across clusters: four live matcha clusters each led with 'matcha latte'. Hypotheses that lead with the same product query are now merged (evidence, phrases and refinements joined; 15 hypotheses became 12, matcha latte 13 posts from 4 clusters), and a hypothesis's id follows its lead query rather than the run's refinement terms: across three live snapshots, the 7 leads found in all of them kept identical ids. The snapshots share most of their 3-day window, so this shows stable identity, not trend persistence

Hypotheses now carry recurrence against the previous snapshot of their query: the same lead id again, and how many of its posts that snapshot had not captured. Live, two matcha snapshots 30 minutes apart (273 mentions, 16 posts not captured before, none dropped): the topic and 'matcha latte' recurred with 16 and 1 such posts, 'iced matcha latte' was a new lead, and 10 leads recurred on the same posts only, which is the same evidence seen again, not continued attention

Stored Open Prices runs now attach to the hypotheses whose product queries they answer (newest run per query, same capture mode). Live: 'matcha latte' carries two products' US shelf medians (14.99 and 9.99 USD), and 'matcha ice cream' records a search that found no priced product; NO_PRICE_EVIDENCE stays open on both, because a shelf price is not a marketplace price

ai_agent_policy_note.finding: Four sites read in this record refuse AI agents in robots.txt (www3.nhk.or.jp, news.yahoo.co.jp, techcrunch.com, www.theverge.com: Claude-User, ChatGPT-User, Perplexity-User, ClaudeBot and/or anthropic-ai disallowed for /). They were read before ECDEV honoured such refusals; robots allowed the ECDEV agent itself. Only counts and hashes are kept here, no content. ECDEV now refuses those fetches (ROBOTS_REFUSES_AI_AGENTS) and the tools no longer read them.
